tiles.name: START
tiles.note: Collect a salary each time you pass. Amount is a guess (₱200).

tiles.name: Calamba
tiles.note: José Rizal was born in Calamba, Laguna on 19 June 1861, the seventh of eleven children of Francisco Mercado and Teodora Alonso.

tiles.name: Biñan
tiles.note: In 1870 Rizal was sent to Biñan, Laguna for formal schooling under Maestro Justiniano Aquino Cruz.

tiles.name: Ateneo
tiles.note: Rizal studied at the Ateneo Municipal de Manila from 1872 to 1877 and earned his Bachiller en Artes with the highest marks.

tiles.name: UST
tiles.note: Rizal took philosophy and letters, then medicine, at the University of Santo Tomas from 1877 before leaving for Spain in 1882.

tiles.name: Intramuros
tiles.note: The walled city of Manila, home in Rizal's day to both the Ateneo Municipal and the University of Santo Tomas.

tiles.name: Dapitan Exile
tiles.note: Works like jail (confirmed rule). Rizal was exiled to Dapitan from 1892 to 1896 after founding La Liga Filipina.

tiles.name: Madrid
tiles.note: At the Universidad Central de Madrid Rizal finished his licentiate in medicine in 1884 and in philosophy and letters in 1885.

tiles.name: Barcelona
tiles.note: Rizal's first stop in Spain in 1882. There he wrote the essay 'El Amor Patrio', his first article written abroad.

tiles.name: Paris
tiles.note: In 1885 Rizal trained in ophthalmology in Paris under the noted eye surgeon Dr. Louis de Wecker.

tiles.name: Heidelberg
tiles.note: In 1886 Rizal worked at the eye clinic of Dr. Otto Becker in Heidelberg and wrote the poem 'A las Flores de Heidelberg'.

tiles.name: Berlin
tiles.note: Noli Me Tangere was printed in Berlin in March 1887, paid for with a loan from his friend Maximo Viola.

tiles.name: Leitmeritz
tiles.note: In May 1887 Rizal visited Leitmeritz, Bohemia to meet Ferdinand Blumentritt in person, his closest friend and correspondent.

tiles.name: Café Rest
tiles.note: A free space where nothing happens (confirmed rule).

tiles.name: London
tiles.note: In 1888 to 1889 Rizal copied and annotated Morga's 'Sucesos de las Islas Filipinas' at the British Museum in London.

tiles.name: Ghent
tiles.note: El Filibusterismo was printed in Ghent, Belgium in 1891. Valentin Ventura's help rescued the printing when Rizal ran out of money.

tiles.name: Hong Kong
tiles.note: Rizal practised as an eye doctor in Hong Kong in 1891 to 1892 before returning to Manila.

tiles.name: Relief Map
tiles.note: In Dapitan Rizal and the Jesuit Fr. Francisco Sanchez built a relief map of Mindanao in the town plaza. It still stands.

tiles.name: Talisay Home
tiles.note: Rizal's farm and home at Talisay, Dapitan, where he lived during his exile, later with Josephine Bracken.

tiles.name: Dapitan School
tiles.note: Rizal ran a school for local boys in Dapitan, teaching them languages, sciences and practical skills.

tiles.name: Quiz Corner
tiles.note: Answer a quiz question. A right answer pays ₱100 (confirmed rule).

tiles.name: Noli: San Diego
tiles.note: San Diego is the fictional town in Noli Me Tangere where Ibarra returns. It is often said to be modelled on Calamba.

tiles.name: Fili: Binondo
tiles.note: In El Filibusterismo, Simoun's lamp bomb is set at the wedding feast in Capitan Tiago's old house on Calle Anloague, Binondo.

tiles.name: Ibarra's School
tiles.note: In the Noli, Ibarra plans a school for San Diego in memory of his father. Elias saves him from a plot at the cornerstone ceremony.

tiles.name: Fort Santiago
tiles.note: Rizal was held at Fort Santiago before his execution. 'Mi Último Adiós' was smuggled out of his cell hidden in an alcohol lamp.

tiles.name: Bagumbayan
tiles.note: Rizal was executed by firing squad at Bagumbayan on 30 December 1896. The site is now Rizal Park (Luneta).
